_comment: Read by scripts/check-postgrest-caps.mjs (findings §17/§18). Every UNBOUNDED read the scanner finds must have a sites entry stating why it cannot silently truncate at PostgREST's 1,000-row cap; every watch runs a live exact count and fails above maxRows (thresholds at 80% of the cap so the check reddens BEFORE truncation begins). Do not register a new site without a reason that names the bound.

lib/catalog.ts::catalog_products::0.reason: Hand-rolled .range() KEPT deliberately: fetchProductsPage loops in fetchCatalogRaw ('while (lastPageLength === PAGE_SIZE)') AND retries transient statement timeouts (57014) with backoff, which fetchAllRows does not — this read runs at build time under 13-way collect concurrency and blocked a Vercel deploy without the retry (findings §16, commit f71c65d). Loop verified by the per-partner built-page counts: 1,454 pages from a 1,454-row table at PAGE_SIZE 250.

lib/catalog.ts::partners::0.reason: partners table, one row per partner (7 today). Grows ~1/import; watched.

lib/pricing/refreshPrices.ts::feed_statu.reason: feed_status filtered on is_catalog_source=true (8 of 9 rows today). One row per feed; grows ~1/import; watched on the whole table, which bounds any filter of it.

lib/supabase/queries.ts::wishlists::0.reason: getWishlistByUser — per-user .eq(user_id) read. Bounded by one user's saved items; a user with >1,000 items would see a truncated list (cosmetic, their own view only). Whole-table watch reddens long before any single user can hold 1,000 rows.

components/PriceHistoryChart.tsx::price_.reason: Schema-bounded: filtered to one (product_id, retailer) over LOOKBACK_DAYS=90, and the table PK is (product_id, retailer, recorded_date) — at most one row per day, so <=90 rows per read regardless of table size (16,201 total when audited). No watch: the bound is structural, not a count.

partners-total.onCross: lib/catalog.ts's partners read will start silently truncating at 1,000 — page it with fetchAllRows before then.

feed_status-total.onCross: refreshPrices' feed-selection read will start silently truncating at 1,000 — page it; a missing feed_status row makes the refresh silently skip that partner's catalog source.

wishlists-total.onCross: getWishlistByUser's per-user bound is no longer safely below the cap in aggregate — re-audit per-user maximums and page the read.

current_prices-total._whyNotEightHundred: The 800 truncation-guard was VOID as written and would have blocked every deploy after the 2026-08-19 11:00Z refresh, including the deploy that fixed it. All five current_prices sites are paged, .maybeSingle-bounded, or head:true counts (getEffectivePrice.ts:70 paged, :126 maybeSingle, refreshPrices.ts:682 paged, :707 upsert, refresh-prices/route.ts:103+115 counts) — no unpaged reader survives §18, so no read can truncate at 1,000 and 800 guarded nothing. Raising it to a bigger fixed number would only move the meaningless number, so the threshold now encodes a real invariant instead.
current_prices-total._whatItGuardsNow: The orphan-override invariant. current_prices is keyed (product_id, retailer) and for real partners retailer IS the product_id's own partner prefix, so the table holds AT MOST one row per catalog product. A count materially above catalog_products therefore means override rows for products that no longer exist — the zombie class of findings §9x (38 such rows deleted 2026-08-18, invisible to MAX-based freshness). The 1.1 multiplier is headroom for the transient window between a product leaving the catalog and its override being cleaned.
current_prices-total._measuredPrediction: Predicted 1,152 rows after the 2026-08-19 11:00Z refresh, measured in advance by replicating the matcher offline against live feed F2639 (scratch/predict-aaawave-match.ts): aaawave deep links carry ued=, not p=, so extractAwinProductId returns null on both sides and all 500 match by name; 500 matched, 500 priced. 652 + 500 = 1,152, against a derived threshold of ceil(1454 x 1.1) = 1,600.
current_prices-total.onCross: current_prices holds more rows than the catalog it overrides — orphan/zombie override rows (findings §9x). Identify override rows whose product_id is absent from catalog_products and decide deliberately whether to delete them; do NOT raise this multiplier to clear the light.

catalog_products-total.onCross: fetchCatalogRaw pages correctly at any size; this watch guards the gzip cache-item tripwire's headroom instead (findings §16) — at ~4,000 rows the compressed snapshot approaches Next's 2MB data-cache item cap. Check the [catalog] console.error tripwire and shrink the snapshot.
